newsitem.title: DENMARK: Bang & Olufsen sees higher 96/97 profits.
newsitem.headline: Bang & Olufsen sees higher 96/97 profits.

text.p: Upmarket Danish audio, video and television manufacturer Bang & Olufsen on Wednesday posted first half 1996/97 pre-tax profits of 174 million crowns ($27.6 million), 32 percent up on the same year-ago period.
In its report, the company -- 25 percent owned by Dutch giant Philips -- forecast a 19 percent better whole year profit and said that business was being boosted by strong growth in the United States.
"We expect turnover to increase by more than 10 percent with the pre-tax and minorities result to be around 325 million crowns for full year 1996/97," B&O said.
It said that it had targeted an annual rise in earnings of at least 15 percent and turnover growth of at least five percent per year in 1996/97 and 1997/98.
The company said that turnover in the 1996/97 first half was up 16 percent year-on-year, at 1.550 billion crowns.
B&O's whole year 1995/96 pre-tax and minorities result was 272 million crowns on 2.717 billion crown turnover.
It said it planned to launch a new audio-visual product and loudspeaker in unnamed markets in April 1997 in keeping with its previously declared aim of introducing a new product concept every year.
B&O said that its audio-video division, the group's biggest operation with 1.405 billion crown turnover in the six months to November 1996, had enjoyed growth in all markets.

It said the United States market showed the greatest growth, rising by 52 percent, while sales in the relatively untried Italian market crept up 31 percent and turnover in Britain rose 26 percent, all measured in Danish crowns.
B&O said its biggest market remained Germany but that growth there was only five percent up in the first half of the year while sales at home in Denmark were up 14 percent up.

It said its telecoms division had the biggest growth rate at 52 percent, boosted by increased sales of mobile, cordless and regular telephones and telecommunications, while its technology division, which produces medical equipment, reported 44 percent growth in the period.
